questions.stem: Kestrel's grader models questions as sealed interface Question permits MultipleChoice, ShortAnswer, TrueFalse with records for each. A colleague adds a fourth record Ordering to the permits list. What happens to switch (q) { case MultipleChoice m -> ...; case ShortAnswer s -> ...; case TrueFalse t -> ...; } used as an expression?
options: It compiles and throws MatchException at run time for Ordering
It no longer compiles: the switch expression is not exhaustive over the sealed hierarchy
It compiles and returns null for Ordering
It compiles only if a default branch already exists elsewhere in the class
questions.explanation: Pattern-matching switch over a sealed type must be exhaustive; adding a permitted subtype makes every exhaustive switch without a default a compile error, which is exactly why sealed types plus switch are safer than visitor or instanceof chains.

questions.stem: The quiz-generation endpoint makes a blocking 2-6 s HTTPS call to Gemini per request. Under load the Tomcat pool of 200 threads is exhausted while CPU is at 15%. Which TWO changes address the cause on Java 21 and Spring Boot 3.2+?
options: Set spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true so each request runs on a virtual thread
Raise -Xmx to 8 GB
Use a reactive or async HTTP client, or keep the blocking client and let virtual threads park while waiting
Wrap the call in synchronized to serialise it
Lower the JDBC pool size to free threads
questions.explanation: The threads are parked on network I/O, not computing. Virtual threads make blocking cheap (the carrier thread is released while waiting), or an async client avoids holding a thread at all. Watch for pinning (synchronized blocks around I/O on older JDKs) and keep an outbound concurrency limit so you do not just move the queue to Gemini's 429s.

questions.stem: A learner-facing record QuizItemLearnerView(Long id, String stem, List<String> options) is built from the entity's mutable ArrayList. What is the risk and the idiomatic fix?
options: None: records are deeply immutable
The record holds a reference to the mutable list, so later changes leak in; copy defensively in the compact constructor with List.copyOf(options)
Records cannot hold collections; use an array
Mark the field transient
questions.explanation: Records make the fields final, not the objects they point to. A compact constructor with options = List.copyOf(options) gives an unmodifiable snapshot (and rejects nulls).

questions.stem: The catalog API returns a 500 with a stack trace when an author posts a duplicate course slug. Which design gives a correct result even when two authors submit the same slug at the same instant?
options: Check findBySlug() before insert and return 409 if present
A unique constraint in the database, mapped from DataIntegrityViolationException to a 409 problem detail, with the pre-check kept only for a friendly message
Synchronize the controller method
Retry the insert until it succeeds
questions.explanation: A select-then-insert check races; only the database can enforce uniqueness across concurrent transactions and other writers. Map the violation to 409 in one @RestControllerAdvice.

questions.stem: V1__catalog.sql is applied in every environment. You need a unique constraint on course.slug. What is the correct move with Flyway?
options: Edit V1 and run flyway repair in every environment
Add V2__course_slug_unique.sql; on PostgreSQL, find and clean duplicates first and build the index concurrently
Let Hibernate ddl-auto=update add it
Drop and recreate the schema in production
questions.explanation: Applied migrations are immutable: Flyway validates checksums and the deploy fails if V1 changes. New changes go in new versions; on a large live table use CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (non-transactional migration) and then attach the constraint.

questions.stem: The progress endpoint loops over enrollments, then course.getLessons(), then queries attempts per lesson. A learner in 8 courses of 15 lessons triggers 137 SQL statements. Which fixes keep the statement count constant? Choose TWO.
options: A JPQL fetch join (or @EntityGraph) for enrollment, course and lessons
Raise the Hikari pool size
A single grouped aggregate query for attempts per lesson for the learner
Enable spring.jpa.open-in-view
Set hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=16
questions.explanation: Fetch joins load the graph in one statement and a GROUP BY tally replaces the per-lesson queries. Batch fetching reduces the count by a factor but still grows with data; open-in-view hides lazy loading rather than removing it; the pool is a symptom.

questions.stem: Which statement about spring.jpa.open-in-view is accurate?
options: It is false by default in Spring Boot 3
It defaults to true, keeps a persistence context open for the whole web request so lazy loading in views and serializers silently issues queries, and Boot logs a warning about it
It only affects Spring WebFlux
It disables the second-level cache
questions.explanation: Boot keeps the historic default of true and warns at startup. Turning it off makes lazy loading outside a transaction fail loudly, which surfaces N+1 problems during development.

questions.stem: The Angular app consumes 400 errors from the catalog API. Which response shape gives the client a stable contract for field errors?
options: text/plain with the exception message
application/problem+json (RFC 9457) with type, title, status, detail and an errors array of {field, message}
HTTP 200 with {"ok": false}
A redirect to an error page
questions.explanation: Problem details are a standard media type; a stable type URI and an errors extension let clients switch on the problem and map messages to form controls. Spring Boot 3 supports ProblemDetail and spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled.

questions.stem: You stream tutor tokens from Spring MVC to the browser. Which return type is the standard building block in Spring MVC (not WebFlux)?
options: ResponseEntity<String> built after the model finishes
SseEmitter (or ResponseBodyEmitter), sending events as tokens arrive from the model client
A @Scheduled method that polls the model
DeferredResult<List<String>>
questions.explanation: SseEmitter writes text/event-stream asynchronously from another thread; set a timeout, complete on done, completeWithError on failure, and handle client disconnects so you stop paying for tokens nobody reads.

questions.stem: The tutor agent calls the catalog API with a Google-signed ID token. What does the Spring Boot side configure to validate it?
options: HTTP Basic with the service account email
spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server with the issuer (and JWK set) configured, plus an audience check for the API's URL and an authorization rule on the caller's email
A shared API key in a header
CORS allowed origins
questions.explanation: The resource server validates signature, expiry and issuer from the JWK set; add an audience validator and authorize by the caller identity. Cloud Run IAM in front is the first layer.

questions.stem: Spec-driven development with an agentic coding tool on this codebase: which practice makes the agent's output verifiable?
options: Let the agent write code first, then generate the spec from it
Write acceptance criteria the agent can check itself (tests, schema rules, status codes), review the plan, then have it implement and run the checks before claiming done
Ask the agent to be careful
Disable tests so the agent moves faster
questions.explanation: Spec, plan, tasks, implementation, each reviewed; acceptance criteria that are executable (like the hidden tests in w1-c1) separate 'the model said so' from verified outcomes. Hooks can enforce running them.

questions.stem: A learner clicks lesson 2 then lesson 3 on a slow connection; lesson 2's response arrives last and replaces lesson 3's quiz. Which RxJS operator on lessonId$ gives latest-wins and cancels the in-flight HttpClient request?
options: mergeMap
concatMap
switchMap
exhaustMap
questions.explanation: switchMap unsubscribes the previous inner observable when a new value arrives; for HttpClient that aborts the request. mergeMap keeps all (last to arrive wins), concatMap queues, exhaustMap ignores new values while busy (right for a submit button).

questions.stem: Which operator fits a quiz Submit button so double clicks never post twice while the first request is in flight?
options: switchMap
exhaustMap
mergeMap
debounceTime alone
questions.explanation: exhaustMap ignores new source values until the current inner observable completes. switchMap would cancel the first POST, which may already have reached the server.

questions.stem: In a standalone component the store exposes state$ (an Observable). What is the idiomatic way to read it in a signal-based template?
options: Subscribe in ngOnInit and never unsubscribe
toSignal(state$) from @angular/core/rxjs-interop, then read state() in the template
Call state$.value in the template
Use setInterval to copy values
questions.explanation: toSignal subscribes in an injection context and unsubscribes when the component is destroyed; computed() can derive view state from it. For manual subscriptions use takeUntilDestroyed().

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about signals are correct?
options: computed() is lazily evaluated and memoised, recomputing only when a dependency changes
Signals replace HttpClient
effect() is meant for side effects such as logging or syncing to storage, not for deriving state
Writing to a signal inside computed() is the recommended pattern
Signals require zone.js
questions.explanation: Derive state with computed(); use effect() sparingly for side effects. Signals work with or without zone.js (zoneless change detection uses them).

questions.stem: The quiz form must type-check answers as numbers and disallow submit until every question is answered. Which approach matches Angular's typed forms?
options: FormGroup<any>
A FormGroup built with FormControl<number | null> per question and Validators.required, using the form's valid status to enable submit
Template-driven forms with ngModel strings
Store answers in localStorage
questions.explanation: Typed reactive forms infer control value types; nonNullable controls and validators keep the submit gate in the model, not scattered in the template.

questions.stem: You stream tutor tokens into the page. Which TWO choices make the experience accessible?
options: Render the streaming text in a region with aria-live="polite" so screen readers announce updates without interrupting
Move focus to every new token
Provide a way to stop the stream and keep keyboard focus on the input
Animate each character with a flashing color
Disable the input while streaming without telling the user
questions.explanation: A polite live region announces new content without stealing focus; a stop control and predictable focus serve keyboard and screen-reader users. A learning product must work with both.

questions.stem: Why does decoding each fetch chunk with new TextDecoder().decode(chunk) occasionally show a broken character?
options: Fetch corrupts UTF-8
A multi-byte character can be split across chunks; decode with one TextDecoder and { stream: true } so the partial bytes are carried over
TextDecoder only supports ASCII
The server sends Latin-1
questions.explanation: Chunk boundaries fall anywhere in the byte stream. A single streaming decoder keeps incomplete sequences until the next chunk; the same applies to SSE event boundaries, which need a text buffer.

questions.stem: An HTTP interceptor adds the auth header and retries failed requests 3 times. What is the risk for POST /api/lessons/3/attempts?
options: None, retries are always safe
Retrying a non-idempotent POST after a timeout can record the attempt twice; retry only idempotent methods, or send an idempotency key the server deduplicates
Interceptors cannot see POST requests
The retry will change the HTTP method
questions.explanation: A timeout does not mean the server did nothing. Limit retries to GET/PUT/DELETE or make the write idempotent with a key.

questions.stem: Which test setup best fits a framework-free store that wraps HttpClient-like observables?
options: An end-to-end browser test for every case
Plain unit tests with a fake API whose Subjects the test releases in chosen order, plus a few TestBed tests for the component wiring
Snapshot tests of the rendered HTML only
Manual testing with Chrome throttling
questions.explanation: Controllable fakes make races deterministic (respond to lesson 3, then lesson 2). Keep component tests thin; Angular's testing guide covers HttpTestingController for the HTTP layer.

questions.stem: The client-side leak guard redacts the quiz answer from streamed tutor text. Why is the server-side guard still required?
options: It is not; the client guard is enough
Client code can be bypassed (dev tools, another client, the raw API), so the control must live on the server; the client guard is defence in depth and UX
Browsers block regex
Angular strips HTML
questions.explanation: Anything enforced only in the browser is a suggestion. The tutor agent's after-model check (w4-c1) is the control.

questions.stem: The quiz generator uses Gemini controlled generation with responseMimeType application/json and a responseSchema. Which TWO problems can still reach your code?
options: Output that is not JSON at all when the finish reason is STOP
answerIndex pointing at the wrong option, or a sectionId that does not exist in the lesson
Truncated JSON when the finish reason is MAX_TOKENS
A schema with OBJECT type returning an array
Unicode in option text
questions.explanation: The schema constrains shape, not meaning: grounding, giveaways and correctness need a validator. A response cut off at the token limit is incomplete regardless of the schema.

questions.stem: At 09:00 every cohort's batch hits Gemini at once on Standard PayGo and you see bursts of 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Which TWO are appropriate?
options: Exponential backoff with full jitter, honouring Retry-After, with a deadline
Retry immediately in a tight loop
Provisioned Throughput (reserved capacity) for the latency-sensitive tutor path if the volume is predictable
Switch models on every retry
Raise the HTTP client timeout to 10 minutes
questions.explanation: PayGo uses shared capacity, so 429s under load are expected; jittered backoff spreads retries. Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity for the workload that cannot wait.

questions.stem: A Gemini response comes back with a candidate whose finishReason is SAFETY and no content. What should the quiz service do?
options: Index candidates[0].content.parts[0].text and let the exception become a 500
Retry the same request three times
Return a typed blocked result (category, source) the UI can explain, count it per category, and not retry
Lower every category to BLOCK_NONE
questions.explanation: A safety block is a decision, not a transient error. Surface it to authors with a clear message and track it; tune thresholds per category for the audience rather than switching filters off.

questions.stem: A request is rejected before generation: no candidates, promptFeedback.blockReason SAFETY. What does that tell you?
options: The output was filtered
The prompt itself was rated at or above a threshold, so there is nothing to parse; handle it as a prompt-level block
The model is down
The quota is exhausted
questions.explanation: Prompt-level blocks come back as promptFeedback with no candidates. Code must check for it before reading candidates.

questions.stem: Release 2.3 copied the kids product's safety profile (BLOCK_LOW_AND_ABOVE everywhere) into the adult university quiz service. What is the senior fix?
options: Turn all filters off for adults
Separate profiles per product and audience with an owner and review, restore per-category thresholds that fit adult course content, and keep an eval set of lessons that must not be blocked
Ask authors to avoid biology
Retry blocked requests until one passes
questions.explanation: Thresholds are product decisions: one profile for different audiences is the bug. A must-not-block eval set catches regressions in CI.

questions.stem: Which statement about thinking on Gemini 2.5 models is accurate enough for a cost discussion?
options: Thinking tokens are free
Thinking improves quality on hard tasks at the cost of latency and billed tokens; you control it with a thinking budget or level, and tuned or simple extraction tasks often want it minimal
Thinking can only be turned on for Pro
Thinking output is returned verbatim to users
questions.explanation: Thinking is a latency/cost/quality dial. For format-heavy tasks like quiz JSON a small budget is often enough; measure with the same eval set.

questions.stem: The tutor sends the same 40,000-token course chapter with every turn. Which feature reduces cost and latency for that repeated prefix?
options: Raising temperature
Context caching for the large repeated context
Streaming
A larger max_output_tokens
questions.explanation: Context caching stores the repeated prefix so subsequent requests pay a reduced rate for cached tokens and skip re-processing; keep the cached part byte-stable and put per-turn data after it.

questions.stem: Why pin a specific Gemini model version in production config rather than an alias that moves?
options: Aliases are slower
Behaviour, quality and cost change between versions; pinning makes upgrades a deliberate change you run through the eval suite, and you track retirement dates
Pinned versions never retire
Aliases are not supported on Vertex AI
questions.explanation: Model versions have lifecycles and retirement dates. Upgrades go through evals like any dependency bump.

questions.stem: You call Gemini from Spring Boot. When would you pick Spring AI's Google GenAI chat client over the Google Gen AI Java SDK directly?
options: Never; Spring AI cannot call Gemini

When you want Spring abstractions (ChatClient, structured output to Java types, advisors, observability) and portability across providers; choose the SDK when you need every Gemini-specific option first
Only for Kotlin
Only on Cloud Run
questions.explanation: Spring AI adds convenience and integration; the SDK exposes new Gemini features (safety settings, thinking config, caching) as soon as they ship. Know both and why.

questions.stem: Each corrective retry for invalid quiz JSON resends the lesson context. What does that do to cost, and what is the sensible control?
options: Nothing; retries are free
Each retry pays the full input again (most of the cost), so cap validity attempts (for example 3), log tokens per request and track retry rate as a metric
It halves output cost
It only affects latency
questions.explanation: Retries multiply input tokens. Cap them, measure them, and fix the prompt or schema when the retry rate rises.

questions.stem: Model Armor sits in front of the tutor. What is it for?
options: Replacing safety filters
Screening prompts and responses for prompt injection, jailbreaks and sensitive data as a separate policy layer
Caching responses
Tuning models
questions.explanation: Model Armor is a screening service for prompts and responses (injection, sensitive data, harmful content), configured as templates you apply in front of models and agents.
